title: Remove legacy route shims and compress versioned configuration surface
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We will remove a set of legacy route shims and collapse multiple versioned configuration entrypoints into a single normalized surface. The goal is to eliminate historical admin/compat endpoints and flag-driven code paths that complicate rollout routing and runtime kernel selection. This reduces maintenance surface area and prevents regressions when changing rollout logic.

Scope of work:
1) Inventory: assemble full list of legacy endpoints (admin v0/v1), compatibility middlewares, and feature flags that alter routing behavior.
2) Mappings & translation layer: implement a one-time migration mapping that normalizes incoming requests to the new config schema. This lives behind a transient compatibility middleware that can be removed after the migration and can run in shadow mode.
3) Config version collapse: migrate persisted rollout configs and toggle metadata from multi-version records to a single canonical config version (add migration script and backup).
4) Flag removal: stage the deletion of deprecated flags in three phases (shadow, soft-delete, hard-delete).
5) Validation & monitoring: add smoke tests, integration tests (router + runtime), and dashboards to monitor 5xxs, tail latency, and routing mismatch rate during rollout.
6) Rollout plan: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% per region, with 24h observation windows and automatic rollback triggers on SLO regressions.
7) Cleanup: after 100% and 48h stable, fully remove middleware and delete DB compatibility columns; archive migration artifacts.

Why this matters:
- Removes fragile conditional logic in the router that causes subtle tokenization/cache mismatches.
- Simplifies kernel selection paths and enables further batching improvements.
- Lowers operational cognitive load for on-call and future feature rollouts.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: transient routing mismatches causing latency spikes. Mitigation: shadow traffic + canary + rollback thresholds.
- Risk: migration script failing leaving partial configs. Mitigation: snapshot configs, reversible migration, run in dry-run first.
- Risk: unexpected external integrations hitting old endpoints. Mitigation: telemetry for hits to legacy endpoints; extend compat window for partners if needed.

Artifacts & links:
- Migration plan doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RC-27456-config-collapse
- DB migration script (dry-run): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pulls/3124
- Router compatibility PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/481
- Test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tests/tree/main/compatibility/27456

Acceptance criteria:
- No remaining code paths that reference legacy route shims or v0 admin endpoints in the runtime repo.
- All configs are stored in canonical versioned schema and DB migration completed with zero data loss.
- After 72h post-100% rollout, middleware and flag artifacts are removed and relevant dashboards show no regressions.

Next steps (short term):
- Finish inventory and mark flags for shadow phase (owner: Jared).
- Create migration dry-run ticket and schedule test cluster run (target: 2026-03-05).
- Implement canary gating & alert rules in Ops dashboards.
